column3: Directly pairs faith and righteous action with a divinely given welcome, establishing the focus condition and outcome.
Adds repentance to faith and sound action as a route to flourishing.
Repeats the faith-and-righteous-action condition with an otherworldly reception.
Restates the core condition and its favorable divine result, though it is already represented.
The immediate continuation frames the message as good news for the God-conscious, extending the local closing sequence.
Repeats the core condition and a final reward without clarifying affection.
Adds an unbroken recompense for faithful righteous action, but repeats the established pattern.
Assures that a believer's righteous effort is neither denied nor lost.
Reiterates the faithful-righteous condition and enduring reward.
Expands righteous action through prayer and giving, with security as its result.
Supplies a concrete confession of faith but not the righteous action or affection outcome.
Directly parallels God making affection between previously hostile parties, giving the focus a social relational horizon.
Joins faith and righteous action to mawadda, making love a central relational counterpart to the focus.

Pairs return with the Merciful and Loving Lord, directly illuminating divine love alongside restored relation.

Offers the contrary case of claimed association without faith and with futile works.
Names al-Rahman but adds no relational or ethical development.
Sharpens the contrast between those who repair and those who corrupt, supporting the value of righteous action.
Reiterates divine response and increase for believers who do righteous deeds.
Provides only the general divine name al-Rahman.
Repeats the faith-and-righteous-action formula with joy as reward.
Connects repentance and righteous action to a genuine return to God.
Provides a false-worship counterpoint involving al-Rahman, relevant to the focus reading's rejected attachments.

Names Wadd as an inherited idol, directly preserving the counterfeit-attachment contrast.
Only narrates the performers' prostration before their confession.
Frames action as a test of excellence but does not develop faith or divinely made affection.
The promise of ease after hardship shares the making verb but not the focus relation.
Links repentance, faith, righteous action, and continuing guidance under abundant forgiveness.
The assignment of light to heavenly bodies does not clarify the focus.
Rejects worship of gods besides al-Rahman, providing a direct doctrinal boundary for the focus context.
The transformation of green wood into fire is unrelated to faithful action and affection.
Provision and safety do not add to the focus's relational outcome.
God's making of mawadda and mercy gives a concrete relational instance of divinely established affection.
The scene of humbled faces and wrongdoing does not clarify the focus.
Within the same surah, repentance, faith, and righteous action mark departure from a corrupted succession.
Places believers with righteous deeds inside divine mercy, complementing the focus's mercy-grounded outcome.
Assures the believer doing righteous deeds against injustice or deprivation.
The cancellation of works through association supplies a contrary boundary for the focus's faithful action.
Identifies those with faith and righteous action as the best creation, reinforcing their distinct standing.
Its correction of legal and bodily claims does not clarify the focus.
Uses desire for disbelief as a hostile counterpart to divinely formed affection.
Repeats the faith-and-righteous-action pattern with humble return to God.
The warning against excess and anger is not a focused neighbor.
Shows faith and righteous action receiving both good recompense and gentle treatment.
Repeats the core condition with forgiveness and generous provision.
Return to God is present, but the verse's main call does not clarify the focus affection.
Associates believing righteous action with elevated ranks, without a relational outcome.
Repeats the core condition with forgiveness and provision.
The declaration of human loss supplies the immediate contrast resolved by the following faith-and-action verse.
Extends faith and righteous action into mutual truth and patience, giving the focus a durable communal practice.
Adds incorporation among the righteous, a social belonging outcome of faithful action.
The prayer for established worship across descendants does not clarify the focus.
Its self-serving response to mercy is not a focused contrast.
Repeats the faithful-righteous category and its recompense.
A prayer for believers' forgiveness only loosely relates to the focus.
Treats desire as reciprocal compromise, a distant contrary use of the affection root.
Repeats faith and righteous action with blessed return.
The plot against Noah adds no focused development despite the idol context.
Its question about future belief offers only a remote faith contrast.
Repeats the faith-and-righteous-action formula and enduring garden outcome.
The secure city image does not clarify the focus.
Contrasts believing with turning away, without the focus's action or affection.
Assures that good work is not wasted, but repeats the core ethical condition.
Repeats faith, righteous action, and unfailing reward.
The garden parable does not develop the focus relation at this point.
Repeats the promise to believers who do righteous deeds.
The creation statement does not clarify the focus.
The resurrection presentation scene does not clarify the focus.
Repeats faith and righteous action while adding guidance by faith.
The oath by time adds no focused contribution after the adjacent pair.
The warning about punishment is not a focused faith or affection parallel.
Connects Quranic guidance and good news to believers who do righteous deeds.
The classification of righteous and other paths does not clarify the focus relation.
Offers a contrary attempt to postpone righteousness until after wrongdoing.
A communal command of blessing and peace offers a secondary social bond among believers.
Its prediction about corrupt descendants does not clarify the focus.
The scheduled destruction of towns is unrelated to the focus relation.
Repeats the believer-righteous-action promise beside punishment for denial.
The denial of divine spouse or child does not clarify the focus.
The travel scene supplies no focused ethical or relational parallel.

Repeats the faith-and-righteous-action entry into gardens.
Names God as the Forgiving, Loving one, directly grounding the focus's affection in divine character.
Contrasts evil deeds with faith and righteous action, preserving their moral distinction.
The succession-and-testing scene does not clarify divinely made affection.
The weighing scene does not add to the focus relation.
Presents God as protector of the righteous, adding a sustained relation to righteous people.
The rejection of ransom for persistent denial does not clarify the focus.
Bodily testimony about deeds is not a focused neighbor.
The assertion of resurrection and complete knowledge does not clarify the focus.
The accounting record of deeds does not develop faithful action's affectionate outcome.

Household etiquette and purity of hearts do not clarify the focus.
The command to follow revelation does not clarify the focus's distinct relation.
The immediate antecedent names false gods sought for honor, directly setting the counterfeit social standing answered by 19:96.
Extends the local reversal: the alleged sources of honor will reject their worshippers and become opponents.
The gathering of the God-conscious before al-Rahman gives the focus a communal reception horizon.
Contrasts rival objects of devotion with believers' stronger love for God, directly clarifying ordered attachment.
Expands righteousness into faith, worship, generosity, fidelity, and patience, supplying its social and practical content.
Joins generous action with ihsan and explicitly states divine love for those who excel in good.
States divine love for those who repeatedly return and purify themselves, closely pairing conduct and divine affection.
Makes following the Messenger the condition through which love for God is met by divine love and forgiveness.
Connects true righteousness to giving from what one loves, specifying a costly social form of good action.
God joins believers' hearts after enmity, a direct communal realization of divinely made affection.
Identifies those who spend, restrain anger, and pardon as recipients of divine love through ihsan.
Links worldly and final good with divine love for those who excel in good.
Names divine love for those who rely on God after mercy and communal consultation.
Specifies beneficent conduct toward kin, neighbors, companions, and the vulnerable as a social field for righteous action.
Calls for cooperation in righteousness and God-consciousness, extending the focus into collective practice.
Directly describes a people whom God loves and who love Him, with humble solidarity among believers.
Combines pardon and overlooking with divine love for those who excel in good.
States that God brought hostile hearts together beyond what material means could achieve, closely paralleling divinely created affection.
Depicts believing men and women as mutual allies through shared moral action and mercy.
Adds the Messenger's concern, compassion, and mercy toward believers as a lived communal expression of care.
Orders justice, ihsan, and care for relatives, supplying a broad social grammar of righteous action.
Links forgiveness and forbearance with support for others under the horizon of divine forgiveness.
Characterizes servants of al-Rahman through humble conduct and peace-making speech.
Frames righteous households and leadership among the God-conscious as a communal fruit of devotion.
Defines believers as siblings and commands reconciliation, directly articulating the social bond suggested by the focus.
Grounds human plurality in mutual knowing and makes God-consciousness the distinguishing measure.
Sets a loyalty boundary by denying that genuine faith can sustain affection for those actively opposed to God and His Messenger.
Shows believers preferring others over themselves, giving concrete communal form to faithful righteous action.
Prays for forgiveness and removal of rancor among believers, directly supporting a divinely maintained loving community.
States divine love for disciplined collective action, adding a communal form of conduct loved by God.
Shows costly feeding of the needy, orphan, and captive as a concrete social expression of righteous action.
Extends faith into mutual patience and mutual mercy, closely fitting the focus's communal affection horizon.
Its refusal to encourage feeding the needy supplies a distant contrary boundary for socially fruitful righteousness.
